column1: # Claims of concepts-fonts-path.svg and the paragraphs around it in docs/concepts/fonts.md.
element
you, at a terminal: vtium config runs as you, and refuses root but for apply
vtium config preview draws a sample of each font, and writes nothing
transition you pick fonts: preview names the fonts new-frit takes
vtium config new-frit makes a font set of the fonts you name
vtium config new-frit --template prints a frit with each key explained
vtium config new-frit --from takes a file you wrote from its template
by hand: the file you write is read as strictly as any frit
transition installing it asks for sudo once
the frit: the directory of frits, /etc/vtium/fonts/
the frit: NAME.vtfrit
the frit names the sources in order
the frit: root owns it, and vtium reads it only after the ownership check
vtium reads the frit, once the frit passes the ownership check that vtium.conf passes
vtium, the console, as root, starts the font helper
the built-in fonts, Unifont and Unscii-8, compiled into vtium
Unscii-8 draws character cells under 16 pixels high
the built-in fonts draw the first frame, and each character the store lacks
the glyph store, in vtium's memory; nothing goes to disk
the glyph store's limit, set by the machine's memory
a full store makes room only for a request for characters on the screen
transition the frit's text goes to the font helper in each request
transition the characters to draw: the screen's, asked first
transition the characters to draw: the fill, while nothing is asked
transition glyphs at the character cell's size; vtium checks each one
transition vtium checks each answer's length before it reads it
vtium-config serve, the font helper
the font helper runs as nobody
the font helper runs in a sandbox
the font helper exits when it has nothing to do
vtium starts a crashed font helper again a limited number of times per boot
font files: the directories where the font helper finds installed fonts
your session: vtium config use-frit NAME
use-frit switches to another font set or to a built-in font
transition OSC 50, through the pty
vtium takes the font that OSC 50 names
vtium switches the console to that font
while allow-font-ops is on, as it is by default
until this session ends: vtium returns the console to the configured font
